definition: Premorbid adjustment refers to how well a person was functioning before the onset of a disorder, especially in social and academic areas during childhood and adolescence. Poor premorbid adjustment is described here as a common precursor to schizophrenia and may reflect underlying neurodevelopmental difficulties.

reasons: The packet supports that poor premorbid adjustment is a frequent precursor to schizophrenia and may reflect neurodevelopmental compromise, but it does not define the term as general pre-onset functioning.

The added detail about social and academic functioning during childhood and adolescence is only indirectly suggested by the study context, not explicitly defined in the source packet as the meaning of the term.
The field is acceptable, but the definition goes beyond what the packet substantiates for a dictionary entry.

The definition describes premorbid adjustment generally as functioning “before the onset of a disorder,” but the packet discusses premorbid adjustment specifically in relation to first-episode schizophrenia spectrum disorders (i.e., as a precursor to schizophrenia), not broadly “before the onset of a disorder.”

The definition claims “may reflect underlying neurodevelopmental difficulties.” While the packet states that childhood trauma interferes with neurodevelopment and that poor premorbid adjustment “may be a manifestation of neurodevelopmental compromise,” the packet does not use the exact framing of “underlying neurodevelopmental difficulties” as the general mechanism of premorbid adjustment itself (it is tied to the trauma–premorbid adjustment pathway).
